title: LRU Cache (Java) - communication round
uncle_hook: Imagine your uncle asks why we cannot just use a regular HashMap and delete old keys manually.
corner_checklist: What happens when capacity is full on put?
Are get and put both O(1)? Why?
Thread safety - do we need it for this problem?
Null keys or null values allowed?
What if capacity is zero or negative?

steps.narration: Thanks for joining. I will drive today - I will type the Java structure and you talk me through your thinking. No need for you to write code. We are building an LRU cache with O(1) get and put.
steps.your_turn: In one sentence for a non-technical friend: what problem does an LRU cache solve?

steps.narration: I will store entries in a HashMap for O(1) lookup. Each value also needs recency order, so I add a doubly-linked list of nodes.
steps.your_turn: Why both HashMap and a linked list? Explain like you are talking to your uncle.

steps.narration: Constructor sets capacity, creates the map, and sentinel head/tail nodes so list operations stay simple.
steps.your_turn: What corner case did I just handle in the constructor? Anything else you would flag?

steps.narration: get returns -1 on miss. On hit, I move the node to the front (most recently used).
steps.your_turn: Walk through get(3) when key 3 exists vs when it does not. Keep it plain language.

steps.narration: put updates an existing key or inserts a new one. If we exceed capacity, evict the tail (least recently used).
steps.your_turn: After put fills the cache, what happens on the next new key? Explain the eviction story simply.

steps.narration: Helper methods unlink a node and splice it at the front, or remove the LRU node before tail.
steps.your_turn: Summarize time complexity for get/put and why. Then name two production corners we did not code (monitoring, persistence, concurrency, etc.).
